item.title: Entire's Git Forge Rethinks Git Collaboration for Coding Agents
item.content:encoded: <img src="https://res.infoq.com/news/2026/11/entire-git-forge-coding-agents/en/headerimage/entire-git-forge-agents-1794134163813.jpeg"/><p>Entire is a Git forge designed specifically for collaboration between human developers and AI coding agents. Its premise is that traditional software development infrastructure, particularly the pull request (PR) model, is not well suited to an environment where AI agents generate, review, and iterate on code at high speed.</p> <i>By Sergio De Simone</i>

item.title: Google Cloud Adds Self-Managed VMware Cloud Foundation on Bare Metal
item.content:encoded: <img src="https://res.infoq.com/news/2026/11/google-cloud-self-managed-vmware/en/headerimage/generatedHeaderImage-1793604325753.jpg"/><p>Google Cloud has made a self-managed VMware solution generally available, running VMware Cloud Foundation 9.x on dedicated Z3 bare metal with root access across ESXi, vCenter and NSX in 22 regions. It sits beside the Google-managed VMware Engine and matches customer-operated offerings from AWS and Oracle, shifting lifecycle, patching and Broadcom licensing back to the customer.</p> <i>By Steef-Jan Wiggers</i>

item.title: Cloudflare Scales D1 Control Plane to Millions of Databases
item.content:encoded: <img src="https://res.infoq.com/news/2026/11/cloudflare-d1-control-plane/en/headerimage/generatedHeaderImage-1792577891694.jpg"/><p>In a recent article, Cloudflare shared the redesign of the control plane of its D1 serverless SQL database to support millions of databases, avoiding centralized bottlenecks, implementing retries and idempotency, and using eventual consistency.</p> <i>By Renato Losio</i>

item.title: How Grab Improved Mobile App Stability by Safely Handling Surge in AI-Generated Code Changes
item.content:encoded: <img src="https://res.infoq.com/news/2026/11/grab-ai-generated-code-safety/en/headerimage/momentic-postgres-clickhouse-1794048104353.jpeg"/><p>The growing adoption of AI coding assistants has accelerated development and increased the volume of code changes per release, bringing more opportunities for defects and crashes, says Grab. To address these challenges, they implemented a layered defense strategy to prevent, detect, and contain crashes throughout the development and release lifecycle.</p> <i>By Sergio De Simone</i>

item.title: Open Source pg_vectorsearch Brings More Scalable Vector Search to PostgreSQL
item.content:encoded: <img src="https://res.infoq.com/news/2026/11/postgresql-vector-search/en/headerimage/generatedHeaderImage-1792331528868.jpg"/><p>Tiger Data has released pg_vectorsearch, an open source PostgreSQL extension for vector similarity search, currently in alpha. Its PRISM index uses data partitioning and compression instead of the graph-based approach used by pgvector’s HNSW index, reducing memory requirements and index build times.</p> <i>By Renato Losio</i>

item.title: Varlock Releases Bumpy: A File-Based Versioning Alternative to Changesets
item.content:encoded: <img src="https://res.infoq.com/news/2026/11/bumpy-changesets-alternative/en/headerimage/generatedHeaderImage-1793973539308.jpg"/><p>Bumpy is an MIT-licensed, TypeScript tool for version management and changelogs in monorepos. It follows the changesets workflow, using markdown bump files, and adds support for workspace and catalog protocols, custom publish commands, and branch-based prereleases. Changesets v3, released in August 2026, closed many earlier gaps, though differences remain.</p> <i>By Daniel Curtis</i>

item.title: Yelp Combines Native and Server-Driven UI for Its AI Assistant
item.content:encoded: <img src="https://www.infoq.com/styles/static/images/logo/logo_bigger.jpg"/><p>Yelp combines native mobile controls with server-driven conversation rendering in its AI Assistant using the CHAOS framework. The architecture separates view configuration from conversation data, supports backend-driven chat interactions, and enables faster UI updates without new app releases. Yelp also discusses cross-platform challenges and reuse for its Biz Ask Anything pilot.</p> <i>By Leela Kumili</i>

item.title: GitLab 19.5 Makes Agentic Development a Governed Part of the DevOps Platform
item.content:encoded: <img src="https://res.infoq.com/news/2026/11/gitlab-19-5-agentic-platform/en/headerimage/generatedHeaderImage-1793095997884.jpg"/><p>GitLab 19.5, released on October 15, puts agentic software development and governance at the centre of the platform, making its GitLab MCP server generally available while expanding how external AI agents can interact with GitLab.</p> <i>By Craig Risi</i>

item.title: TypeScript 7.1 Beta: Restores the Compiler API and Makes Vue and Svelte First-Class
item.content:encoded: <img src="https://res.infoq.com/news/2026/11/typescript-7-1-beta/en/headerimage/generatedHeaderImage-1793901816316.jpg"/><p>TypeScript 7.1 Beta, announced October 20, 2026, restores the compiler API removed in 7.0, now split into separate entry points. It adds content mappers, letting tools like Vue check non-standard files. One Vue project's type checks fell from 14.19 to 3.10 seconds. An editor issue remains open, and teams may need TypeScript 6 alongside 7.</p> <i>By Daniel Curtis</i>

item.title: Presentation: The Socio-Technical Staff+ Engineer: Architecture, Culture and Organisational Change
item.content:encoded: <img src="https://res.infoq.com/presentations/sociotechnical-staff-engineer-architecture/en/mediumimage/medium-1792066457983.jpg"/><p>Vanessa Formicola shares how technical leaders can move beyond "wishful architecture" by practicing holistic socio-technical engineering. She discusses why engineering leaders must account for organizational maturity, reward structures, geopolitical climate, and team dynamics, framing the staff-plus role as designing the conditions for technology to thrive rather than just picking tools.</p> <i>By Vanessa Formicola</i>

item.title: AWS Ships Continuum for Code Vulnerabilities
item.content:encoded: <img src="https://res.infoq.com/news/2026/11/aws-continuum-ga/en/headerimage/generatedHeaderImage-1792886107294.jpg"/><p>AWS has made Continuum for code vulnerabilities generally available in two regions. The service proves exploitability by running real exploits in a sandbox, then opens fixes as pull requests. Published pricing charges per finding processed as well as per line of code, and practitioners are asking what would justify letting it merge fixes on its own.</p> <i>By Steef-Jan Wiggers</i>

item.title: Vault Fork OpenBao Adds External Keys and Quantum-Ready TLS
item.content:encoded: <img src="https://res.infoq.com/news/2026/11/vault-fork-openbao-27/en/headerimage/generatedHeaderImage-1793734932785.jpg"/><p>OpenBao has released version 2.7, adding read scaling for PostgreSQL-backed deployments, support for external hardware security module (HSM) and key management service (KMS) keys, and post-quantum cryptographic algorithms. The release also introduces control groups for human review of sensitive operations and new headers intended to keep requests consistent across load-balanced OpenBao nodes.</p> <i>By Matt Saunders</i>

item.title: GitHub Actions Lockfiles Reach GA to Secure Workflow Dependencies
item.content:encoded: <img src="https://res.infoq.com/news/2026/11/github-actions-lockfiles-ga/en/headerimage/generatedHeaderImage-1793888107988.jpg"/><p>GitHub has made workflow dependency lockfiles for GitHub Actions generally available on October 28, 2026, two weeks after the feature entered public preview. Workflows can maintain clear tag and branch references.</p> <i>By Claudio Masolo</i>

item.title: Article: Identity as an Architectural Concern: Enterprise IAM Beyond Authentication
item.content:encoded: <img src="https://res.infoq.com/articles/identity-as-architecture/en/headerimage/identity-as-architecture-header-1793629959196.jpg"/><p>The way you design your identities will drive your data models, your service scope, and your revocation policies; enterprise identity management is thus an architectural problem, not an afterthought. Based on our experience in service account governance, this article touches upon graph vs. RBAC, integrating a vault you don't own, and bounding revocation latency for an event stream.</p> <i>By Vaishnavi Khosla</i>

item.title: Edera's Object Capability Bounded Authority Promises to Isolate Credentials from AI Agent Workloads
item.content:encoded: <img src="https://res.infoq.com/news/2026/11/ai-credentials-isolation/en/headerimage/generatedHeaderImage-1793853184587.jpg"/><p>Edera announced Object Capability Bounded Authority, a security model that separates an AI agent's or MCP server's required authority from the credentials behind it. Hypervisor-enforced capabilities limit agents to specific actions without storing secrets in the workload. Initial releases cover scoped command execution and workload identity; credential-brokered API access will follow.</p> <i>By Olimpiu Pop</i>

item.title: Leapwork Play Reaches GA with Governance for Playwright Tests
item.content:encoded: <img src="https://res.infoq.com/news/2026/11/leapwork-play-playwright/en/headerimage/header-1793826326573.jpeg"/><p>Leapwork Play adds requirement traceability and approval workflows around portable Playwright tests. Full governance and audit capabilities require an enterprise package.</p> <i>By Mark Silvester</i>

item.title: Presentation: Zero Trust Agent Systems that Pass Audits and Still Ship
item.content:encoded: <img src="https://res.infoq.com/presentations/zero-trust-ai-agents-production-security/en/mediumimage/advait-patel-medium-1792655207658.jpeg"/><p>Advait Patel shares a playbook for securing AI agent systems in production. He discusses moving defense boundaries from the prompt to the tool layer, enforcing scoped workload identities, and mitigating prompt injection via tool outputs. He explains how to structure audit-ready observability and implement kill switches to protect critical data while keeping deployment fast and compliant.</p> <i>By Advait Patel</i>

item.title: Amazon ECS Gateway Arrives with Generated Hostnames and No Custom Domain Support
item.content:encoded: <img src="https://www.infoq.com/styles/static/images/logo/logo_bigger.jpg"/><p>AWS has released Amazon ECS Gateway, an account-level ingress resource letting platform teams define networking once and application teams opt services in with a connector. Each service gets a generated hostname and routing is host-based, and neither the announcement nor the documentation covers custom domains.</p> <i>By Steef-Jan Wiggers</i>

item.title: Docker Urges Isolation and Governance for AI Agent Security
item.content:encoded: <img src="https://res.infoq.com/news/2026/11/docker-ai-agent-security/en/headerimage/generatedHeaderImage-1793733720293.jpg"/><p>Docker has published a guide to five security risks that arise when AI agents are allowed to browse, run code and call tools with limited human oversight. They argue that the autonomy that makes agents useful also makes conventional application security controls insufficient. The company positions isolation and governance, rather than model improvements alone, as the main defences.</p> <i>By Matt Saunders</i>

item.title: LinkedIn Uses OpenTelemetry to Trace the Member Journey from Tap to Backend
item.content:encoded: <img src="https://res.infoq.com/news/2026/11/linkedin-opentelemetry-journey/en/headerimage/generatedHeaderImage-1793095474316.jpg"/><p>LinkedIn has built an OpenTelemetry-based telemetry platform that connects what members do in its iOS, Android, and web applications with the backend services processing those interactions.</p> <i>By Craig Risi</i>

item.title: Shopify Overexposed Scans GKE Ingresses and Cloud Run for Exposure
item.content:encoded: <img src="https://res.infoq.com/news/2026/11/shopify-kubernetes-ingresses/en/headerimage/generatedHeaderImage-1793520999206.jpg"/><p>Shopify has introduced Overexposed. This internal scanner locates Kubernetes Ingresses on GKE and Cloud Run services. It checks for those that are accessible from the internet without authentication.</p> <i>By Claudio Masolo</i>

item.title: AWS Capacity Largely Sold out through 2027, with On-Demand Headroom Reserved
item.content:encoded: <img src="https://res.infoq.com/news/2026/11/aws-capacity-sold-out/en/headerimage/generatedHeaderImage-1793124716899.jpg"/><p>Amazon CEO Andy Jassy says AWS’s large committed cloud capacity is largely sold out through 2027, with part of 2028 already allocated, while the company continues to reserve headroom for On Demand, EC2 and Bedrock. Practitioners discussing the remarks report difficulty obtaining On Demand capacity for ordinary EC2 instances, and similar constraints at other providers.</p> <i>By Steef-Jan Wiggers</i>

item.title: File Mover Express: AWS Releases Open-Source Tool for S3 File Transfers
item.content:encoded: <img src="https://res.infoq.com/news/2026/11/aws-s3-file-transfer/en/headerimage/generatedHeaderImage-1792218946629.jpg"/><p>AWS has recently released File Mover Express, an open-source application under the Apache 2.0 license for transferring large files between local systems and Amazon S3. Available for macOS, Windows, and Linux, it supports parallel transfers, automatic performance tuning, retries, pause and resume, and file integrity verification.</p> <i>By Renato Losio</i>

item.title: Chrome Opens Trial for the Email Verification API: Letting Sites Verify without Sending Emails
item.content:encoded: <img src="https://res.infoq.com/news/2026/10/chrome-email-verification/en/headerimage/generatedHeaderImage-1793091215457.jpg"/><p>Google has opened a Chrome origin trial for the Email Verification API, a WICG proposal that lets the browser confirm email ownership without sending a message. Gmail is the first provider. Developers add form hints and validate a signed token server-side. Commenters question the privacy benefit, and the API is best used as a progressive enhancement.</p> <i>By Daniel Curtis</i>

item.title: Cloudflare and VoidZero Introduce tsrs: an AI-Generated Rust Port of TypeScript
item.content:encoded: <img src="https://res.infoq.com/news/2026/10/cloudflare-tsrs-ai-typescript/en/headerimage/generatedHeaderImage-1793039825386.jpg"/><p>Cloudflare, VoidZero and Max Schwenk announced tsrs, an experimental Rust port of the TypeScript compiler, built with the TypeScript team's involvement. Cloudflare claims up to 8x faster checking and 70% less memory than TypeScript 7.0, though one test against 7.1 beta showed 2.7x. It lacks watch mode and a language server, and exits with code 2 on type errors.</p> <i>By Daniel Curtis</i>
